exposure: Anomalous origin of the right subclavian artery (AORSA) from the right pulmonary artery
outcome: Surgical correction of AORSA and d-TGA
cohort: A single newborn diagnosed with anomalous origin of the right subclavian artery and d-transposition of the great arteries in the first hours of life.
finding: A very rare case of anomalous origin of the right subclavian artery coexisting with d-transposition of the great arteries was successfully diagnosed and surgically corrected in a newborn.
